title: Tensor-closure no-go for universal finite dimension selectors
statement: Under ordinary finite-dimensional tensor composition, any admissible system-dimension set S closed under composition and containing d>1 must contain d^k for all k>=1 and is therefore infinite. In particular, a universal singleton selector {3}, or any finite selector containing 3, cannot include composites as systems of the same class.
tested_dimensions: 1-12 exhaustively for pair products; singleton fixed points checked through 256; analytic theorem covers all positive integers

edge_cases.dimension_1: {1} is tensor closed and is the unique positive-integer singleton fixed point
edge_cases.irreducible_only_rule: not ruled out; selector may apply only to atomic/irreducible sectors
edge_cases.resource_quotient: not ruled out when effective dimension is not faithful and multiplicative
edge_cases.alternative_direct_sum: also defeats a globally fixed nonzero dimension because d+d>d

prior_art_boundary: Dimension multiplicativity under tensor products and monoidal dimension functions are standard. GPT reconstruction literature treats composite-system structure and multiplicative capacities/dimensions explicitly. No novelty claim is made for the underlying theorem.
pdt_consequence: A defensible PDT derivation of n=3 must be formulated at the irreducible/primitive sector level, or must derive a nonstandard effective composition law. It cannot assert that every composite distinction space itself has dimension exactly 3 under ordinary tensor composition.
open_next: derive a PDT-native irreducibility criterion stable under composition/decomposition
test graded/factor-relative distinction products rather than universal fixed dimension
search for a same-input quantitative PDT deviation with a declared resource window
